success_patterns: Double-meaning 'X or Y' clue ('mouth of the Mississippi or a Helen Reddy "Dawn"'): the agent found one word that fits both halves ('Delta') by using the quoted word as a blank in a song or phrase title ('Delta Dawn'). It did not pick a synonym for just one half.

'Act IV, Scene 1 of this play...' and 'daughter of Hecuba': the agent answered with the entity of the type the clue asks for (the play title 'Henry V', the person 'Cassandra'). It ignored the many anchor names in the passages (Agincourt, Hecuba, Priam).

'one of these bombs': the agent kept the head noun ('hydrogen bomb'), since the bare modifier 'hydrogen' would not name the entity. It matched the phrase that recurs across independent passages together with the clue's date and place.

In all four, the answer was a short, standard, bare form with no descriptor or added qualifiers. Each was confirmed by a phrase repeated across many passages that matched the clue's distinctive words.

patch.reasoning: All four successes were produced by rules already in the skill: type-checking the slot, the head-noun exception, and double-meaning clues. Most of the skill needs no change. The one under-specified pattern is the double-meaning clue where one half contains a quoted word, such as 'a Helen Reddy "Dawn"'. The existing example covers only an idiom ('put to the test'). A short addition to that bullet explains the mechanism the agent used: treat the quoted word as the blank in a title and verify the answer against the other half. It is low risk and does not touch any form rule that stable passes depend on.

edits.target: A dictionary synonym that fits only one half ('trial') is wrong. When passages are noisy, use your own knowledge of sports terms and idioms.
edits.content: - Variant: one half is a title or phrase with a quoted word ('a Helen Reddy "Dawn"', 'the "Jersey" ...'). Treat the quoted word as the neighbor of a blank ('___ Dawn' -> 'Delta Dawn') and test the same blank word against the other half ('mouth of the Mississippi' -> delta). Answer with that single shared word, with no quotes and no part of the title that the clue already states.
